patent_summary: The document discloses a genus of benzoylcyclohexanediones of general formula (I) in which the phenyl ring of the benzoyl group carries at its 3-position the substituent -L-R1, where L is a C1-C6 alkylene chain and R1 an optionally substituted hydrocarbon radical that may additionally contain phosphorus, oxygen, sulfur, nitrogen or halogen, R2 to R5 are independently hydrogen, hydroxy, thio, amino, cyano, nitro, halogen or such a hydrocarbon radical, R6 and R7 are each drawn from their own separate lists, and Y and Z are divalent units within the cyclohexanedione ring itself, taken from O, S, N-H, N-alkyl, CHR7 and C(R7)2, with Z also able to be a direct bond. It also sets out general schemes for preparing these compounds and their application, alone or in a mixture with formulation auxiliaries, as herbicides and plant growth regulators.
novelty_claims: Claim 1 positions the formula (I) genus itself as new, subject to the express proviso that "-L-R1 is not to stand for optionally substituted CH2-O-phenyl when R2 and R3 are each chlorine and R4 and R5 are each hydrogen", which carves the genus away from the phenoxymethyl-substituted benzoylcyclohexanediones of the cited art. The background objects that the 3-position-bridged benzoylcyclohexanediones already known from JP-A 08 020554, JP-A 02 00222, WO 99/10327, WO 99/07688 and WO 99/03845 have activity that "is not always sufficient, or, where the herbicidal activity is sufficient, undesirable damage to the crop plants is observed", and states the object of the invention as compounds "which overcome the disadvantages known from the prior art", so the positioning is on selectivity between weeds and crops as much as on structure. The remaining claims extend this to herbicidal compositions (claim 8), to compositions in a mixture with formulation auxiliaries (claim 9), to a process for controlling undesired plants by applying an effective amount to the plants or their locus (claim 10), and to use in crops of useful plants including transgenic crops (claims 11 to 13). Note that although the title and the abstract both state that processes for preparing the compounds are described, the claim set contains no preparation process claim.
